title: Bezos Predicts a Three-Day Workweek. Amazon Just Cut 30,000 Jobs.
source_used: Yahoo Finance article on a Fox News interview
key_facts: Jeff Bezos made the forecast in a Fox News interview with Bret Baier aired 7 Oct 2026.
He said AI productivity gains could reach double digits, letting some people support a family on a three-day week.
He framed it as a personal vision, not Amazon policy, and gave no timeline or calculation.
Baier asked about Amazon cutting about 30,000 corporate roles since late 2025 (about 14,000 in late 2025, 16,000 in January 2026, per Amazon and Reuters).
Bezos pointed to pandemic-era overhiring as the main cause; the coverage does not establish that AI played no role.
quote_evidence: Bezos made his forecast in an interview aired October 7, 2026, on Fox News with anchor Bret Baier.
Bezos did not provide a timeline, a distribution model, or any calculation showing how those productivity gains would flow to workers rather than to employers or shareholders.
why_it_matters_hint: A leading tech founder's optimistic forecast sits beside his own company's job cuts, with no plan shown for how gains reach workers.
notes: Interview aired 7 Oct, before the 8 Oct window start; score lowered one. Credit goes to the Fox News interview; Yahoo Finance relays and comments.
